headline: Seven in ten Americans now expect artificial intelligence to reduce the number of jobs in the country over the next 20 years, a survey by Pew Research Center found.
score_reason: Large, multi-country survey with a clear rise in worry; it measures expectations, not jobs lost.
importance_line: Public fear of AI job losses is rising, most among young adults and in the US, though the survey records opinion rather than actual employment changes.
source: Radio Ink, citing Pew Research Center
summary: Radio Ink reports, citing Pew Research Center, that 71% of Americans expect AI to mean fewer jobs over the next 20 years, up from 64% in August 2024, with only Australia and South Korea (76% each) more pessimistic among 37 countries surveyed. Pew also found 52% of Americans are more concerned than excited about AI in daily life, and adults aged 18 to 34 are now slightly more concerned (55%) than those 50 and older (53%).
notes: Pew's own report not opened; figures from Radio Ink.
